name: Sex-Role Scripts
oneLine: Steiner and Wyckoff's structural account of how boys are trained toward an over-built Adult and a Nurturing Parent switched on only for others, while girls are trained toward a strong Nurturing Parent and a suppressed Adult - in both cases, at the cost of the Natural Child.
whatYouDid: You named Marcus's exhausted, help-refusing week as the male sex-role script, rather than 'just a strong work ethic' or a single driver flashing by.

fromBook.quote: men are enjoined against being in touch with their Natural Child. They are given messages not to feel, to discount their feelings... Men, were they tuned in to their feelings, would not only be unable to exploit others, but they'd also be unable to exploit themselves.

expand.definition: This chapter's analysis is by Hogie Wyckoff. The claim is structural, not a personality judgment: which ego states a person is trained and permitted to use is scripted along gender lines before any individual content (injunctions, drivers) gets added on top.
expand.otherFraming: Steiner credits Wyckoff's chapters on sex-role scripting as the origin of his whole category of 'banal scripts' - the political analysis of gender came first, and the general theory of banal, everyday scripts generalized from it.
expand.tryThisToday: Notice one moment today where you default to an ego state because of sex-role training rather than because it's actually the most useful one for the situation - and try the other one on purpose.
